articles.full_text:
A waterlogged street in Kochi.
| Photo Credit: H. VIBHU
The intensity of rain has significantly subsided in Kerala with the weakening of the active monsoon conditions. However, heavy rainfall is likely to continue in parts of the State for a couple of more days, influenced by the cyclonic circulation over the Bay of Bengal.
An orange alert has been issued for seven districts – Kasaragod, Kannur, Ernakulam, Idukki, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, and Alappuzha – on Thursday, warning of very heavy rain. The other seven districts have been placed under a yellow alert for isolated heavy rain.
According to a weather bulletin issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the heavy and isolated heavy rainfall activity will continue in parts of the State for a few more days under the combined influence of the upper air cyclonic circulations that persist over South Interior Karnataka and neighbourhood; south coastal Tamil Nadu and Puducherry; and over Southeast Bay of Bengal.
No extreme heavy or very heavy category rain was reported anywhere in Kerala during the last 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday (August 5). Panathur in Kasargod recorded the highest rainfall of 9 cm during this period, followed by Thodupuzha and Udumbannoor in Idukki and Muliyar in Kasargod with 7 cm each. Meanwhile, swell waves with 1.2-1.4 m height are forecasted until Thursday night at various parts of the State including Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam and Alappuzha coast. As there is a possibility of surging of waves during this period, fishermen are advised to operate boats with utmost vigilance, and recreation activities have to be done with due care.

Shimla, Aug 5 (PTI) The Shimla MeT office on Wednesday issued a yellow alert for heavy rain in isolated places across Himachal Pradesh till August 11.
A total of 112 roads are closed for vehicular traffic while 61 water supply schemes and 189 transformers were disrupted as of Wednesday evening, according to the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC).
A maximum of 37 roads were blocked in Mandi, followed by 34 in Kullu, 29 in Sirmaur, eight in Kangra, four in Shimla, two in Una and one in Chamba district.
A devotee from Punjab was killed after a heavy stone crashed through the sunroof of the SUV he was travelling in near Mehla on the Chamba-Bharmour road in Himachal’s Chamba district in the wee hours of Wednesday morning.
According to the police, the boulder came down the hill and struck the top of the SUV, hitting one of the occupants directly.
The deceased, identified as Makhan Singh (40), a resident of Hoshiarpur in Punjab, was declared brought dead by the doctors at Pt Jawaharlal Nehru Government Medical College and Hospital, Chamba.
The vehicle with people on board was en route to Bharmour to undertake the Manimahesh yatra. The other three passengers were safe. The body was sent for a post-mortem examination, and family members of the victim have been informed about the tragedy, police said.
Heavy to very heavy rain lashed parts of the state in the past 24 hours since Tuesday evening, and Jatton Barrage received 135.4 mm, followed by Raipur Maidan 124.2 mm, Naina Devi 110.6 mm and Nahan 101.2 mm.
Dehra Gopipur received 97.2 mm rain, Nahan 64.8 mm, Nadaun 90 mm, Kangra and Ghamroor 76.2 mm, Murari Devi 66.6 mm, Dharamshala 60.1 mm, Neri 58.5 mm, Una 52 mm and Poanta Sahib 50.2 mm.
Thunderstorms and lightning lashed Kangra district. Kukumseri was coldest at night, recording a low of 13.2 degrees Celsius, while Una was hottest during the day with a high of 34.2 degrees Celsius. PTI BPL MPL MPL

Italy puts 27 cities on highest heat alert as temperatures top 40°C
Authorities warn of worsening health risks as another heatwave grips the country, with three suspected heat-related deaths and heightened wildfire concerns.
Italy placed 27 cities under its highest heat alert on Wednesday as another intense heatwave gripped the country, with several deaths suspected to be linked to the soaring temperatures.
According to ANSA news agency, 25 cities were under a red alert on Wednesday, with the number expected to rise to 27 on Thursday as temperatures continue to climb.
ANSA reported three suspected heat-related deaths: a 40-year-old carpenter who fell ill while working on a rooftop, a 55-year-old security guard who suffered a medical emergency while sitting in a car, and a 90-year-old woman who collapsed while in a garden.
Temperatures are forecast to exceed 40°C in parts of the country, with only a slight drop to 36-39°C expected over the weekend.
Authorities also remain on alert over the heightened risk of drought and wildfires. Fires have been reported in Marsica, in the central region of Abruzzo, while firefighters continue battling a blaze in the Karst area near Trieste that has been burning since Saturday.
